what: Which address lines the ASIC decodes on the DSP's I/O bus, measured by sending the mailbox to folded port numbers
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2
method: probe_transport --port-fold, delivered to supervisor RAM at 0x3000 with ATGLK2W (2104 word writes per image, all verified byte-exact against diagnostic-ram.bin before arming), started by pointing IVT vector 8 at 0000:3000 and setting T0CON.INT at 0xff36 from 0x8021 to 0xa021. The kernel is the resident's own outbound mailbox sender; only the two port numbers in it change between runs.

runs.name: control
runs.means: the delivery, launch, DSP download and mailbox all work; the negative results below are informative

runs.name: A4 fold
runs.means: A4 is NOT decoded by the ASIC: a mailbox sent to 0x4e/0x4f arrives exactly as one sent to 0x5e/0x5f

runs.name: A5 control
runs.result: CDRP1 START then CDRP1 ERR TAG - nothing arrived
runs.means: A5 IS decoded: the fold is specific to bit 4, not the ASIC ignoring the address bus

conclusion: The ASIC decodes A0-A3 and A5 on the DSP's I/O cycles, and does not decode A4. This confirms the board readings of pins 55-58, 59 and 60 by their electrical effect.
corroborates: docs/dsp-pin-probes.md, which reported A0-A3 and A5 connected and A4 absent from visual inspection
emulator: The harness predicted the opposite for the folded run - it compared `port == 0x5E` and returned CDRP1 ERR TAG. Fixed in bridge.ASIC_DSP_PORT_MASK; all three runs now reproduce the board's frames byte for byte.
caveats: The first fold run reused the control's payload pattern, so its frame was indistinguishable from a re-run of the kernel already in DSP program RAM. It is not counted; the run recorded here uses pattern 0xf700 and its frame carries it, which is what shows the freshly downloaded kernel ran.

Bits 6 and 7 of the port number were not tested. The decode is known to include A0-A3 and A5 and to exclude A4; whether A6/A7 are decoded is still open, so ASIC_DSP_PORT_MASK models the decode as possibly narrower than the board's.

emit_ram_writes.py's arm.txt only hooks IVT vector 8. On this board that starts nothing, because T0CON has EN=1 and INT=0 - timer 0 runs but never interrupts. Every run here needed the separate ATGLK2WFF36,A021.
The monitor restores IVT vector 8 when it completes, so a second run needs the vector written again. The first fold attempt produced no output for this reason.
The board was left with vector 8 restored to 8000:108F and T0CON back to 0x8021, and answers AT normally. The placed image is still in RAM at 0x3000-0x406f and is inert; a power cycle clears it.
